title: Knight Hops
statement: A chess knight stands on square (0, 0) of an n × n board, with rows and columns numbered from 0. Return the fewest knight moves to reach square (row, col). Every square can be reached when n >= 4 or the target is the start.

answerKey.pattern: BFS over squares, with the eight knight moves as edges
keyPoints: Each square is a vertex; a knight move is an edge
Every move costs one, so BFS finds the fewest moves
Stop as soon as the target is taken from the queue
edgeCases: A corner next to the start
acceptableSlowerApproaches: DFS with a depth limit: exponential
A formula: exists for infinite boards but breaks near edges

hints: What are the vertices and edges here?
Squares are vertices; the eight L-shaped jumps are edges, all of cost 1.
BFS from (0, 0), stepping only onto squares inside the board.
